claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you assess your eligibility for Child Benefit. To get started, I need to gather some information about your circumstances and children.

Let me begin with a few basic questions:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. My son Alex is 18 and he's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful. So Alex is 18 and in college studying A-levels.

**Can you confirm that you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. Now I need to understand your living arrangements with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you in Manchester, or does he live elsewhere (for example, in student accommodation at or near his college)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. That's very helpful to know.

**Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there anyone else (such as his other parent or another family member) who might also be claiming or could claim for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm the only one claiming. His other parent isn't claiming anything for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a good understanding of your situation now. Let me confirm the key details:

- You have one child: Alex, who is 18 years old
- Alex is in college studying A-levels (approved education)
- Alex lives with you in Manchester
- You're the only person claiming Child Benefit for him
- You live in the UK

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you should qualify for Child Benefit for Alex. The rules state that you normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 20 who stays in approved education or training. Since Alex is 18, living with you, and in full-time approved education (A-levels at college), he meets the criteria.

However, I have one final question to ensure there are no other circumstances affecting eligibility:

**Does Alex currently receive any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit? Or does he work 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually Alex does receive Universal Credit in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. I need to clarify this further, as it may affect your eligibility.

**Can you tell me approximately how much Universal Credit Alex receives per week, and has he been receiving it for a while, or is this something recent?**

This will help me understand whether this disqualifies you from claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact weekly amount off the top of my head, but he's been receiving it for a few months now. He applied for it himself to help with his costs while he's studying.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context. This is an important detail for your eligibility.

According to the Child Benefit rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts getting certain benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit. Since Alex is receiving Universal Credit in his own name, this means **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him**.

The fact that he's still in approved education (A-levels) doesn't override this rule - the receipt of Universal Credit in his own right is a disqualifying factor.

Let me now provide you with my final eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex at this time because he is receiving Universal Credit in his own name.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future and he stops receiving Universal Credit, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. If that happens, you would need to make a new claim. I'd recommend contacting HMRC if you have any questions about this or if Alex's situation changes.
